text: To answer your IPO query: with a $10 (Rs 960) budget, you cannot participate in mainboard IPOs like Srit India or Shah Investor's Home, as they require a minimum application of roughly Rs 14,000–15,000 per lot. Even if you could, IPOs are not a shortcut to 10x; listing gains are volatile, and after accounting for the 20% short-term capital gains tax, your net return would be significantly lower. Regarding Reliance on Zerodha, buying a single share would cost you the share price plus roughly Rs 18 in statutory charges and DP fees, which is a massive 1.8% drag on a Rs 1,000 position before the stock even moves. NVDA remains a high-quality, high-margin play, but at a 63.6% decade CAGR, it is a long-term compounder, not a 10x lottery ticket.
